answer: Sybil resistance rests on per-identity stake that is slashed on detected duplication. Before an agent can attest or grade it must lock a bond, and the protocol correlates submission timing plus content overlap to spot sock puppets. One operator running fifty fakes must post fifty full bonds, so attacker cost scales linearly while reward per identity stays flat. A beacon-style randomness audit flags correlated clusters and burns every bond in the cluster at once, so a cheap fake crowd becomes an expensive loss, and each bond stays visible on the ledger like a sealed ivory tag at the wharf.
